entry_points.name: close_account
entry_points.note: Loads the user row, calls anonymize_user and commits; no row is deleted.

stores.name: users

fields.name: metadata_json
fields.note: The column comment says the client sets arbitrary key/value pairs and that support pastes contact details in here.

erasure.note: anonymize_user writes only email and full_name; metadata_json is never overwritten or deleted.

fields.name: deleted_at
fields.note: Column the application would use to mark a row closed; no code in the repository writes it.

erasure.note: close_account does not set deleted_at and no other module writes the column.
close_account overwrites email with its SHA-256 hash and full_name with the constant "removed"; the row and its primary key survive, and the hashed email still points back to the person.

stores.note: Table holding the account record for each user.

stores.name: tickets

fields.name: notes
fields.note: The column comment says the free text may contain phone numbers.

erasure.note: The only deletion path anonymises two columns on the user row and deletes nothing, and the User.tickets relationship carries no cascade string, so ticket rows keep their subject, notes and user_id.

stores.note: Table holding support tickets, each carrying a foreign key to users.id.

stores.name: request_log

fields.name: path
fields.note: The requested URL path is logged on the same line as the caller's IP address.

erasure.note: No code in the repository removes or rotates entries written by log_request, and the account-closing route does not touch the log.

stores.note: Python logger that writes the client IP address and request path for every request.
